author: Morris Leader
title: First responders save elderly man during Lake Hopatcong rescue drill
text:
Christine Myers Commissioner Director | Official Website
Christine Myers Commissioner Director | Official Website
An ice rescue training exercise at Lake Hopatcong quickly shifted to a real emergency response when first responders saved an 82-year-old man who fell through the ice. The event took place during a joint training session involving the Morris County Sheriff’s Office, N.J. State Police, Mt. Arlington Police Department, Hopatcong Police Department, and N.J. Division of Fish and Wildlife Conservation Police.
Morris County Sheriff James M. Gannon remarked on the significance of their work: “It is work like this, with our other public safety partners, that makes it all worth it. Responding in a time of need and applying our training to help an individual who is in dire consequences, all with positive outcomes. Saving lives is the purpose of our mission and the reason why we train together and ensure seamless performance.”
The man was reported to have fallen through the ice near Lake Hopatcong Yacht Club on Bertrand Island while operating an iceboat. Sgt. Edward Koster from the Sheriff's Office Marine Unit, Sgt. Nicholas Vernotica from the Patrol Division, Cpl. Ivan Bajceski and Sheriff's Officer Ryan Wood from the Emergency Services Unit (ESU), along with N.J. State Police Marine Bureau personnel responded promptly.
As three Mt. Arlington firefighters approached across unstable ice to reach him, Sgt. Koster and Cpl. Bajceski arrived at the scene with the Sheriff’s ESU truck to meet with Mt. Arlington Fire Department's incident commander.
Sgt. Vernotica and Officer Wood deployed a MARSARS Ice Rescue Sled using the Sheriff's Heavy Rescue Truck to assist in retrieving the victim who remained conscious but needed urgent help.
The rescuers worked cautiously across the fragile surface to maneuver toward him as he lay partially submerged in broken ice beside his vessel which had sunk partially into icy water.
